open_points.subject: A10 agent-authority checks
open_points.text: “every agent-authority call is checked three times by Registry” conflicts with “'Register an agent session' is checked for the token only” and with session operations that are checked for the first two conditions only
open_points.question: Do all agent-authority calls require three checks, or do registration and non-project session operations use the stated one- and two-check exceptions?
options: Apply three checks to every call
Apply one check to registration, two to session operations and three to project operations
Rename the decision so the exceptions are not contradictory
open_points.default_guess: Apply the explicit exceptions in the normative rules.

open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read ... and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes and deployment boundary implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that browser cookies are scoped by host and path rather than full origin and may be sent to another port on the same host?
options: Require a dedicated Registry hostname and a host-only Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie
Use host/path scoping and rely on CSRF protection for other same-host origins
Treat every origin on Registry's host as trusted
open_points.default_guess: Require a dedicated hostname and a host-only Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation expiry
open_points.text: “It is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes”
open_points.question: Is a confirmation value accepted or refused at exactly its shown instant plus 10 minutes?
options: Valid while now is strictly earlier than shown plus 10 minutes
Valid through the exact 10-minute instant
Use backend timestamp precision to decide
open_points.default_guess: Valid only while now is strictly earlier than the 10-minute deadline.

open_points.subject: A22 removed artifact types after restore
open_points.text: “After the removal, publishing that type ... [is] refused” and “A removed type's name is never declared again” conflict with A18 allowing a restored store to be started by “the release that made it,” which may still declare that type
open_points.question: After a type has been removed by a later release, may restoring an older backup under its original release make that type publishable again?
options: Yes, restore rewinds both store and vocabulary history
No, removed-type tombstones must survive outside the restored store
An old release may read the store but must not serve writes
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restore as a history rewind and use the vocabulary of the release that starts it.

open_points.subject: A16 import file digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm and byte canonicalisation define the file identity used by confirmations, the migration closure and the audit entry?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with SHA-256
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Let each backend choose its digest
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: A16 validation after import renaming
open_points.text: The owner may replace the imported display name, but “A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing”
open_points.question: If a source project has a blank or missing display name but the owner supplies a valid replacement in the mapping, is the project still malformed?
options: Validate the final mapped record, so the replacement cures the source defect
Validate the source first, so the import is refused despite the replacement
Allow replacement only for present nonblank source names
open_points.default_guess: Validate the final mapped record and accept a valid replacement.

open_points.subject: A17 backup location
open_points.text: “The backup location must exist and let Registry create and remove a file in it”
open_points.question: Must the backup location be dedicated to Registry, and how does Registry distinguish its backups and temporary files from unrelated files when checking and deleting them?
options: Require a dedicated Registry-only directory
Define a Registry-owned filename namespace and ignore everything else
Treat every file in the configured location as Registry-owned
open_points.default_guess: Require a dedicated Registry-only backup directory.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and it records “a digest of the key” readable without the key
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption construction, key derivation, nonce format, metadata authentication and key-digest algorithm define a valid backup?
options: Specify a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope and cryptographic key identifier
Delegate the complete format to a fixed release dependency
Permit any backend encryption that prevents plaintext reading
open_points.default_guess: Specify a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with authenticated metadata and a SHA-256 key identifier.

open_points.subject: A18 failed backup verification
open_points.text: “A backup that fails the check is deleted” but “a backup or a deletion that fails ... is tried again at the next run,” while the invariant says “every kept backup is ... checked”
open_points.question: What state results when verification fails and deletion of that invalid backup also fails?
options: Keep it under an explicit invalid/quarantined name that restore never considers
Leave it looking like a normal backup and retry deletion later
Stop serving until the invalid file is removed
open_points.default_guess: Quarantine and mark it invalid, exclude it from restore candidates, and retry deletion.

open_points.subject: A19 query and command structure
open_points.text: “No value a caller gives ever becomes part of a query's or a command's structure; how the store's backend lowers this is the backend's”
open_points.question: Does “structure” prohibit textual interpolation entirely, or only caller control of semantic operators, identifiers and command syntax, and what evidence verifies the rule for the selected backend?
options: Require parameterised data APIs and fixed or allowlisted structure, with backend-specific tests
Permit backend escaping or literal lowering when it preserves data semantics
Trust the backend without a verifiable Registry requirement
open_points.default_guess: Require parameterised data APIs for values and fixed or allowlisted structure, verified for the chosen backend.

open_points.subject: A21 security-review status after A19 change
open_points.text: “A change to a decision a category names reopens this review” conflicts with “Security review: PERFORMED” after A19, named by injection_interpreted_input and browser_boundary, was changed
open_points.question: Is A21 currently reopened and awaiting a new review, or has the changed A19 wording already been reviewed and reaccepted?
options: Mark A21 reopened until the changed rule is reviewed
Record a new performed review that explicitly accepts the change
Treat this wording change as non-substantive despite rule 2
open_points.default_guess: Mark A21 reopened and perform the affected-category review again.

open_points.subject: A21 concurrency review
open_points.text: The concurrency category expressly includes “single-use values,” but its references are only “A01, A04, A07, A12, A14”; the single-use confirmation rule is in A13
open_points.question: Must A13 and its concurrent-consumption guarantee be part of the concurrency review, or is the reference list intentionally non-exhaustive?
options: Add A13 and test that only one concurrent submission consumes and proceeds
Declare reference lists non-exhaustive
Exclude confirmation values from the concurrency category
open_points.default_guess: Add A13 and require atomic consumption so only one concurrent submission proceeds.

open_points.subject: A21 service-token credential abuse
open_points.text: authentication_credential_abuse claims to answer “credential stuffing ... at every human and machine boundary” using A09, A13 and A17, but those decisions state no abuse-control rule for repeated wrong service tokens
open_points.question: What happens when a caller repeatedly presents wrong service tokens?
options: No throttling because tokens are high-entropy and the network boundary is trusted; record that explicitly
Apply a global service-authentication throttle
Throttle separately by presented service identity or connection source
open_points.default_guess: Apply no Registry throttle to service tokens, but state explicitly that high entropy, network restriction and host monitoring are the chosen controls.

open_points.subject: A01 retry racing a correction
open_points.text: A repeat is decided by equality with “that record's current facts,” while only creates sharing a request id are explicitly applied one at a time
open_points.question: If a create retry races a correction of the record it originally created, what linearisation determines whether the retry returns the record or is refused for differing current facts?
options: Serialize the retry and correction; whichever commits first determines the result
Compare with the facts at the retry's transaction start
Bind the request id permanently to the original create facts instead of current facts
open_points.default_guess: Serialize both actions on the record and use commit order.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession uploaded import file
open_points.text: M11 says the uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted,” while A16 says “a file another session keeps stays until that session ends” after an import succeeds
open_points.question: When one owner session accepts the import, are uploaded files in all other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?
options: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the closure is committed
Drop only the confirming session's file and retain the others
End every owner session after a successful import
open_points.default_guess: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the import closure is committed.
